subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Franklin D. Roosevelt was first elected President of the United States in which year?
questions.explain: FDR won the 1932 presidential election and launched the New Deal after his March 1933 inauguration.

questions.q: Martin Luther King was assassinated in Memphis, Tennessee, in which year?
questions.explain: King was assassinated on 4 April 1968 in Memphis.

questions.q: Which 1920s figure led the 'Back to Africa' movement through the Universal Negro Improvement Association?
questions.explain: Marcus Garvey led the UNIA and promoted black pride and a 'Back to Africa' movement in the 1920s.

questions.q: The National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) was founded in which year?
questions.explain: The NAACP was founded in 1909 to combat racial discrimination and segregation.

questions.q: The Compromise of 1877 is most associated with which outcome?
options: The passage of the Civil Rights Act
The end of Reconstruction and withdrawal of federal troops from the South
questions.explain: The 1877 Compromise resolved the disputed 1876 election and led to the withdrawal of federal troops, ending Reconstruction.

questions.q: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, bringing the USA into the Second World War, took place on which date?
questions.explain: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, prompting the US declaration of war.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment, ratified in 1865, abolished slavery in the United States?
questions.explain: The 13th Amendment, ratified in December 1865, abolished slavery and involuntary servitude.

questions.q: Joseph McCarthy's anti-communist crusade, giving its name to 'McCarthyism', reached its height in which period?
questions.explain: Senator McCarthy's prominence peaked in the early 1950s before his censure by the Senate in 1954.

questions.q: In the 1896 Supreme Court case Plessy v Ferguson, the Court established which doctrine?
questions.explain: Plessy v Ferguson (1896) upheld racial segregation under the 'separate but equal' doctrine.

questions.q: The Civil Rights Act outlawing discrimination in public accommodations and employment was signed in which year?
questions.explain: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 banned discrimination on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex or national origin.

questions.q: In which year was the landmark Brown v Board of Education ruling handed down?
questions.explain: The Supreme Court decided Brown v Board of Education in May 1954.

questions.q: Malcolm X, the prominent Black nationalist who broke with the Nation of Islam, was assassinated in which year?
questions.explain: Malcolm X was assassinated in February 1965 in New York City.

questions.q: The Montgomery Bus Boycott, sparked by Rosa Parks's arrest, began in which year?
questions.explain: The boycott began in December 1955 after Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat.

questions.q: The Voting Rights Act, which banned literacy tests and protected black voter registration, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Voting Rights Act of 1965 outlawed discriminatory voting practices used against African Americans.

questions.q: The GI Bill of 1944 chiefly provided what for returning servicemen?
options: Education funding, loans and unemployment pay
questions.explain: The 1944 Servicemen's Readjustment Act (GI Bill) funded veterans' education, home loans and unemployment benefits.

questions.q: The 15th Amendment, which barred denial of the vote on grounds of race, was ratified in which year?
questions.explain: The 15th Amendment was ratified in 1870, prohibiting voting discrimination based on race.

questions.q: The Wall Street Crash, which triggered the Great Depression, occurred in which month and year?
questions.explain: The stock market collapsed in October 1929, with 'Black Tuesday' on 29 October.

questions.q: The 14th Amendment, granting citizenship and equal protection of the laws, was ratified in which year?
questions.explain: The 14th Amendment was ratified in 1868, defining citizenship and guaranteeing equal protection.

questions.q: Martin Luther King delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech at the March on Washington in which year?
questions.explain: King delivered the speech at the March on Washington in August 1963.

questions.q: In which Supreme Court case did the Court rule school segregation unconstitutional, overturning 'separate but equal'?
questions.explain: Brown v Board of Education declared racial segregation in public schools unconstitutional.

questions.q: The crisis over the desegregation of Central High School, requiring federal troops, occurred in which city in 1957?
questions.explain: In 1957 President Eisenhower sent troops to enforce integration at Little Rock Central High School.

questions.q: The National Origins (Johnson-Reed) Immigration Act, which set strict national quotas, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The 1924 Immigration Act established national-origin quotas that heavily favoured northern and western Europeans.

questions.q: President Lyndon B. Johnson's domestic reform programme of the mid-1960s was known as what?
questions.explain: Johnson's 'Great Society' programme aimed to end poverty and racial injustice, creating Medicare and Medicaid in 1965.

questions.q: In which year did the assassination of Abraham Lincoln take place, just days after Lee's surrender at Appomattox?
questions.explain: Lincoln was shot by John Wilkes Booth on 14 April 1865 and died the following day, shortly after the Civil War ended.

questions.q: The Selma to Montgomery marches, which helped galvanise support for voting rights, took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Selma marches of March 1965 dramatised the struggle for the vote in the South.

questions.q: The Black Panther Party, advocating self-defence and black empowerment, was founded in 1966 in which city?
questions.explain: Huey Newton and Bobby Seale founded the Black Panther Party in Oakland, California, in 1966.

questions.q: The Social Security Act, introducing federal old-age pensions, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Social Security Act of 1935 created old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.

questions.q: The Wagner Act of 1935 is significant because it did what?
options: Guaranteed workers' rights to unionise and bargain collectively
questions.explain: The 1935 Wagner (National Labor Relations) Act protected the right of workers to organise and bargain collectively.

questions.q: The Tennessee Valley Authority, a key New Deal agency providing electricity and flood control, was created in which year?
questions.explain: The TVA was established in 1933 as part of FDR's First New Deal.

questions.q: Medicare and Medicaid, providing health coverage for the elderly and poor, were established in which year?
questions.explain: Medicare and Medicaid were created in 1965 as part of Johnson's Great Society.
